title: Contrastive learning
reading: The slide frames supervised classification as a form of contrastive learning. It decomposes a standard network into two parts: the classifier, which is the weight matrix of the final fully-connected layer, and the features, which are the representations produced just before that layer. The implication is that comparing features against class weight vectors is itself a contrastive comparison, so ordinary supervised training already performs the kind of pull-together/push-apart operation contrastive methods make explicit.
